Rationalize

/RASH-uh-nuh-lyz/ - the stress falls on RASH · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Rationalize means to invent reasonable-sounding excuses for a choice or behavior.

She rationalized skipping the reunion — too far, too formal — though the truth was a quarrel she didn't want to reopen.

Worked Example

After cutting the rookie, the manager rationalized the decision all winter: the kid was “a bad fit,” the roster “too crowded,” the timing “out of my hands” — every reason arriving conveniently after the choice, and none of them the misjudged tryout he never mentioned.

Rationalize is the accusing word here because the reasons were invented afterward to make a finished decision feel sound. Explain would be neutral; justify would mean the reasons were honestly good. Rationalize says the logic is decoration — reasonable-sounding, and reverse-engineered.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

excuse: An excuse admits a fault and offers a reason meant to lessen the blame for it. To rationalize is to deny there was a fault at all: invented reasons dress the choice up as sensible. Excusing asks for pardon; rationalizing insists none is needed.

justify: To justify is to argue honestly that the act was actually right, with reasons that are real and were true before the choice was made. Rationalize is its dishonest twin: the reasons arrive afterward and exist to flatter the chooser. Good reasons justify; manufactured ones rationalize.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

confess: to state the real reason plainly, blame and all

admit: to accept an unflattering truth about yourself

Where it sits · how deliberately the truth gets bent — explain → rationalize → whitewash

explain vs. rationalize: To explain is milder than to rationalize — an explanation lays out what happened honestly, while rationalizing starts bending the reasons to flatter the chooser.

whitewash vs. rationalize: Whitewash goes further than rationalize: a rationalizer half-believes the excuses, while a whitewasher knowingly paints over the wrongdoing for others.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — ration

Root — ration: a reckoning, a calculation — later, reason itself (Latin ratio)

Suffix — -al

Suffix — -al: relating to

Suffix — -ize

Suffix — -ize: to make

Put it together

Put it together: Ration (a reckoning, Latin ratio) + -al + -ize = to make something look reasoned. The irony is built in: a rationalized choice wears the costume of calculation, but the arithmetic was done after the decision, not before it.

Use the root in a new word: ration

Use the root in a new word: ration: The lifeboat's water ration was two cups a day, measured to the drop.

Word Choice

everyday, quietly critical

Rationalize almost always accuses: the reasons came after the choice, and they flatter the chooser. If the reasons are honest and good, the fair word is justify — a distinction this card's Quick Check leans on.
